items.title: Black Basta Ransomware Leader Added to EU Most Wanted and INTERPOL Red Notice
items.description: Ukrainian and German law enforcement authorities have identified two Ukrainians suspected of working for the Russia-linked ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group Black Basta. items.title: Let’s Encrypt has made 6-day IP-based TLS certificates Generally Available
items.description: Let’s Encrypt, a key provider of free TLS certificates, has rolled out short-lived and IP address-based certificates for general use. These new options became available starting in early 2026, addressing long-standing issues in certificate security. items.title: Argus – Python-powered Toolkit for Information Gathering and Reconnaissance
items.description: Argus is a comprehensive Python-based toolkit designed for reconnaissance tasks in cybersecurity. The developers recently released version 2.0, expanding it to include 135 modules. This tool consolidates network analysis, web app scanning, and threat intelligence into one interface. items.title: Google’s Vertex AI Vulnerability Enables Low-Privileged Users to Gain Service Agent Roles
items.description: Google’s Vertex AI contains default configurations that allow low-privileged users to escalate privileges by hijacking Service Agent roles. XM Cyber researchers identified two attack vectors in the Vertex AI Agent Engine and Ray on Vertex AI, which Google deemed “working as intended. items.title: Tennessee Man Pleads Guilty to Repeatedly Hacking Supreme Court’s Filing System
items.description: Nicholas Moore pleaded guilty to repeatedly hacking the U.S. Supreme Court’s filing system and illegally accessing computer systems belonging to AmeriCorps and the Department of Veterans Affairs. The post Tennessee Man Pleads Guilty to Repeatedly Hacking Supreme Court’s Filing System appeared first on SecurityWeek.
